matchstick.title: Check arithmetic validity
matchstick.principle: After proposing a transformed equation, compute the integer values of both sides using standard Roman numeral conversion and verify they are equal.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately before finalizing the answer, to ensure the move actually solves the puzzle.
matchstick.example: Accepting a transformation that still leaves the equation false because the arithmetic was not re‑checked.

matchstick.title: Match‑stick orientation matters
matchstick.principle: A stick’s orientation (vertical, horizontal, diagonal) is fixed; you may only place it in a location that requires the same orientation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever moving a stick, ensure the target position expects the same orientation.
matchstick.example: Turning a vertical stick into a diagonal, producing an invalid numeral shape.

matchstick.title: Limit changes to two characters
matchstick.principle: A single stick move can affect at most the source character (which loses a stick) and the destination character (which gains a stick).
matchstick.when_to_apply: During planning, ensure you do not inadvertently alter a third character.
matchstick.example: Attempting to change three characters by moving one stick, leading to multiple invalid changes.

matchstick.title: Transform numerals via single stick moves
matchstick.principle: Use known one‑stick transformations (e.g., I↔II, V↔X) that keep both source and destination characters valid after the move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When moving a stick between numerals, check that both resulting characters are standard Roman numerals.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from V to I and ending up with a non‑standard shape.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: The final output must be a single line that starts with ‘Correct version of the equation:’ followed by the transformed equation, with uppercase letters and collapsed whitespace.
matchstick.example: Providing the answer without the required prefix or with extra lines, causing the verifier to reject it.

matchstick.title: Accurate parsing of the original equation
matchstick.principle: Read the given equation carefully and record each numeral and operator exactly as they appear before attempting any transformations.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving the puzzle.
matchstick.example: Misreading the original equation and moving a stick from the wrong character.

matchstick.title: Within‑character diagonal repositioning
matchstick.principle: You may relocate a diagonal stick within the same numeral, effectively turning X into V (or V into X) without affecting other characters.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a diagonal can be repositioned to change a numeral shape while staying within the same character.
matchstick.example: Leaving a diagonal in place and missing the opportunity to turn X into V.

matchstick.title: Operator conversion via vertical stick relocation
matchstick.principle: Adding a vertical stick to a ‘‑’ creates a ‘+’, and removing the vertical stick from a ‘+’ yields a ‘‑’.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to change a minus to a plus (or vice versa) by moving a vertical stick.
matchstick.example: Changing a minus to a plus without moving the vertical stick from any source, resulting in an extra stick.

matchstick.title: Operator swapping via horizontal stick relocation
matchstick.principle: You can move a horizontal stick from the equality sign to a minus sign (or vice versa), turning the equality sign into a minus sign and the minus sign into an equality sign, effectively swapping them while preserving a valid equality.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation can be corrected by swapping ‘=’ and ‘‑’, as in turning ‘XVII = X - VII’ into ‘XVII - X = VII’.
matchstick.example: Leaving the equality sign unchanged and trying to add a stick elsewhere, missing the chance to swap the operators.

matchstick.title: Allow removal of a single‑stick numeral
matchstick.principle: If a numeral consists of a single stick (e.g., I), moving that stick away eliminates the numeral; this is allowed provided the resulting equation remains syntactically valid and the arithmetic holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When moving a vertical stick from an I to create a new I elsewhere, causing the source I to disappear, as in ‘V = XVII - X’ → ‘VI = XVI - X’.
matchstick.example: Keeping the source I after moving its only stick, leaving an empty character or invalid shape.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the match‑stick move and forgets to recompute the values of both sides.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always recompute the integer values of both sides after any transformation and compare them before answering.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model moves sticks without ensuring the remaining strokes form a recognized Roman numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Check that each affected numeral still corresponds to a valid Roman numeral (or disappears entirely if it loses its only stick).

matchstick.why_it_happens: Sticks are added to or removed from operators without respecting the exact composition required for +, -, or =.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Apply the specific operator conversion rules (vertical stick ↔ plus/minus, horizontal stick ↔ swapping = and -, etc.) and verify the resulting symbol is a valid operator.

matchstick.description: Missing destination for moved stick (effective removal)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a stick from a character but does not specify where the stick is placed.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Every stick removal must be paired with a placement on a valid target character; track both source and destination.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model outputs the solution without the exact required prefix or includes extra lines or whitespace.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Print exactly ‘Correct version of the equation: <equation>’ on a single line, with uppercase letters and collapsed whitespace.
